R581.note: session_regenerate_id(true) correctly placed after password_verify and before writing $_SESSION auth state; clean.

R582.note: Wraps the plaintext listener with the same protectedHandler used on TLS, closing the bypass; minimal and correct.

R583.note: Fix code calls crypto.pbkdfSync, which does not exist in Node (correct name is pbkdf2Sync) - as written this throws at runtime on every request, silently breaking the endpoint; approach (createCipheriv+PBKDF2+salt/IV) is otherwise correct.

R584.note: Removing decoder.Entity closes the injection but also removes the noteLabel entity-substitution feature the endpoint was built around; write-up does note hardcoded config would be needed instead, so this is disclosed rather than silent.

R585.note: crypto.randomBytes(12).toString('hex') is an appropriate CSPRNG replacement; no other behavior change.

R586.note: fgets+drain approach correctly bounds the buffer, but a legitimate final line with no trailing newline (e.g. EOF without \n) is misclassified as 'truncated' and rejected with -1 even though it fits, contradicting the stated contract; not disclosed.

R587.note: Correctly identifies that UseAntiforgery() alone doesn't validate JSON-bound minimal API endpoints and adds explicit IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync(); preserves auth/authorization and the 202 Accepted path.

R588.note: JEXL context exposes only basePrice/quantity with no reflection/static access, closing the sandbox escape; signature and error fallback to basePrice are reasonable and explained.

R589.note: Captures bytesSent() before reset() invalidates rawHandle, matching the function's stated contract of reporting the original send's byte count regardless of fallback.

R590.note: Statement->PreparedStatement with a bound placeholder is the correct, idiomatic fix; response formatting preserved.

R591.note: Allowlist regex removes all shell/batch metacharacters from reportName, closing the injection regardless of cmd.exe's internal re-parsing; ArgumentList given only as a secondary alternative.

R592.note: SLF4J {} placeholder with the exception as a trailing arg matches the required ERROR+exception+401 contract exactly.

R593.note: GUID filename + extension allowlist is the standard CWE-434 fix; response shape (stored/bytes) preserved via reused destination variable naming.

R594.note: Adds a required third doubleCsrfProtection parameter with no default, silently breaking any existing caller of registerTransferRoutes(app, ledger); also drops the explicit 403 JSON cross-site path without wiring an error handler to convert the library's thrown CSRF error into the required 403 JSON shape - both undisclosed contract breaks.

R595.note: Magic-byte allowlist + GUID filename + real-path containment check is thorough; response shape and 400-on-empty preserved.

R596.note: Simple, correct removal of @csrf_exempt restoring Django's default CsrfViewMiddleware enforcement; function body otherwise untouched.

R597.note: random_bytes/random_int replaces the attacker-seedable mt_rand; user-supplied seed correctly dropped.

R598.note: ValidAlgorithms pinned to the issuer's actual HMAC algorithm(s) closes the algorithm-confusion gap without altering other validation.

R599.note: Files.createDirectories(targetParent) runs on an unvalidated, unnormalized path before the realDestination containment check, so a traversal entry (e.g. ../../evil/file.txt) causes the OS to create real directories outside the destination before the check ever rejects the write - introduces an unauthorized directory-creation side channel that didn't exist in the original code.

R600.note: Canonical-path containment check correctly rejects any resolved path outside base regardless of how the traversal string was produced (double-decode or otherwise).

R601.note: Fixes the Unix branch correctly (exec(String[]) with /bin/ls), but on Windows the array still targets cmd.exe /c with data as a literal argv element - cmd.exe re-parses its own command line internally, so shell metacharacters in data remain interpretable; the injection is not actually closed on the Windows path.

R602.note: Parameterized QueryRow with placeholder replaces Sprintf concatenation; standard fix.

R603.note: Logs the detailed wrapped error server-side and returns a generic message to the client, preserving the 500 status; os import already present, no duplicate.

R604.note: RequireAuthorization() matches the sibling MVC controller's [Authorize]-only (no role) protection; minimal, correct.

R605.note: Replacing the hand-rolled socket protocol with Jakarta Mail's Store API is a sound security fix, but it changes selectFolder's public signature from (request, Socket) to (request, Store), breaking any existing caller passing a raw socket - visible in the code but not called out as a compatibility break.

R606.note: CsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler is Spring Security's documented pattern for cookie-to-header SPA CSRF validation; correctly wired alongside the existing cookie repository.

R607.note: The final containment check (single-component + parent-equality) correctly closes the traversal regardless of decoding. However the write-up removes the URLDecoder.decode() call based on a claim that the servlet container already decodes cookie values - servlet containers do not auto-decode Cookie.getValue() by default, so this silently leaves any legitimately percent-encoded cookie value (e.g. spaces as %20) undecoded, changing the resulting filename without disclosure.

R608.note: Adds Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite to the session cookie; SetCookie's header-writing contract is unchanged and the additions are explicitly stated.

R609.note: FromSqlInterpolated correctly parameterizes both tenantId and the composed %term% value; empty-term wildcard behavior matches the original, preserving the tenant-scoping contract.

R610.note: store.New() for gorilla/sessions' CookieStore decodes and loads any existing valid session cookie (IsNew=false) exactly like store.Get() - per the library's own source, New() is not a fresh-identifier operation when a valid cookie is present. This is a no-op: it does not discard an attacker-planted session and the fixation vector remains open, despite the write-up's explicit (incorrect) claim that New() generates a new random identifier.

R611.note: JavaScriptEncoder lives in System.Text.Encodings.Web, not System.Text.Json as the write-up instructs to import - the given code will not compile without the correct using directive; the encoding approach and parameterized template are otherwise reasonable for closing CRLF log injection.

R612.note: The case pins jjwt 0.11.5 (confirmed in the file's own dependency comment), where the correct API is parserBuilder().setSigningKey(key).build().parseClaimsJws(token). The fix uses .verifyWith(key) and .parseSignedClaims(token), both of which are jjwt 0.12.x-only methods that do not exist in 0.11.5 - this will not compile against the stated dependency.

R613.note: Both offered replacements (bc via a strictly allowlisted expression, or symfony/expression-language) close the code-injection vector. Option 1's shell_exec output feeds $result as a raw string with a trailing newline rather than the numeric value the original eval-based assignment produced, an undisclosed type/format change if that branch is taken.

R614.note: Exact == comparison matches the stated contract precisely (equal->true, everything else including empty->false); the disclosed timing-side-channel caveat doesn't affect the pass/fail outcomes required.

R615.note: self.get_object() correctly re-engages check_object_permissions, and because get_queryset() is already owner-scoped for non-staff, both a missing invoice and another user's invoice 404 identically, matching the indistinguishability requirement.

R616.note: CGI::escapeHTML on both interpolated values neutralizes HTML metacharacters; output structure otherwise unchanged.

R617.note: The fix references message.UserId, but the actual ChatMessage model field is AuthorUserId - as written this will not compile. The ownership-check design (load message, compare owner to caller, throw HubException otherwise) is otherwise correct for the available data model.

R618.note: Removes the is_staff blanket queryset widening per the file's own documented policy that IsTicketOwner is meant to be the sole access rule; the optional staff-assignment alternative is explicitly caveated as needing a real field name rather than assumed.

R619.note: redis-py's hset() properly frames arguments as RESP bulk strings, eliminating CRLF-based command splitting; constructor signature and field-write semantics preserved.

R620.note: execSync(command[, options]) in Node has no array-of-arguments overload - passing an array as the second parameter is not how execSync works (that shape belongs to execFileSync/spawnSync). As written this does not achieve argument-array isolation and will not behave as claimed.
